A real vector space is a [[vector space]] $V$ where

$$V \in \mathbb{R}^n$$

It can be written as a set:

{{#content:Q1999}}

== Test conditions ==

A set of vectors $G=\{\vec g_1, \cdot, \vec g_n\}$ is a real vector space if:

* $\vec 0 \in G$, and
* $g_1,\cdots,g_n \in \mathbb{R}^n$, and
* $\sum^{n}_{i=1}\alpha_i g_i \in G$.

== Examples ==

1. Is $G=\{(x,1,y) | x,y \in \mathbb{R}\}$ a vector space?

{{Hidden solution}}
Since $\vec 0=(0,0,0) \notin G$, $G$ is not a vector space.
{{End hidden}}
